newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, EU reach accord on tequila, mezcal origin.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, EU reach accord on tequila, mezcal origin.

text.p: The Mexican government said on Thursday it had won denomination of origin protection for Mexican-produced tequila and mezcal in the European Union.

"This accord is very important for Mexican producers of tequila and mezcal, because as a result of the accord these drinks may only be commercialized in the European Union if they were produced in Mexico," the trade ministry said in a statement.

"From the date the accord comes into effect, the denominations tequila and mezcal will be exclusively Mexican and will be applied solely to those spirits that come from the recognised producer regions in our country and that meet the corresponding quality norms," the ministry said.
"The agreement with Europe will provide legal security to Mexican producers of tequila and mezcal in their second-biggest export market, the European Union," it added.
"Exports of Mexican tequila to Europe are more than $17 million a year, and it is hoped that with the legal protection of this agreement, that figure will rise."

The talks took two years and produced an accord which will be initialed Friday and formally signed in May by Trade Minister Herminio Blanco and EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler, the ministry said.

The accord would allow Mexico to fight "the illegitimate use that certain European producers were making, especially, of the denomination tequila, calling certain European aguardiente spirits tequila", the ministry added. -- Martin Langfield, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9558
